question_types_read: Shell vs. Editor: evaluating an expression in a script does not by itself print the expression value; distinguish it from an explicit print call.

recommended_original_problem_types: Annotate each expression with operand values, declared types, promoted types, common type and intermediate value; distinguish mathematical integers from bounded machine operations.

Contrast casting before integer division with casting its already-truncated result. Include negative operands, a divisor-zero guard and the minimum-signed-value divided by minus-one exception without executing invalid code.
Prove unsigned residue conversion algebraically, then show why signed narrowing and signed arithmetic overflow are different semantic categories.
Derive an overflow-safe positive doubling guard before multiplication, rather than predict outputs from a signed-overflow execution.
Use short-circuit conditions to protect a valid division and show exactly which operand is evaluated; separate logical truth from bitwise operations.
Compare C assignment snapshots, Python scalar bindings and Java assignments through separately labelled, independently worded state ledgers.
Distinguish expression evaluation in a Python file from an explicit print call; do not equate interactive-shell display with language assignment semantics.

Use full mathematical quotient/remainder equations for negative valid C division, then explicitly contrast Python floor-division semantics when that independently verified language rule is introduced.
Derive representability of binary rational fractions and explain why a floating cast or more printed digits cannot reconstruct information lost earlier.

Classify each unsafe fragment before any numeric tracing: constraint violation, implementation-defined result, unspecified order, undefined behavior or a fully defined expression under declared assumptions.
